_comment: Short descriptions used ONLY by scripts/build-skill-zips.py, for the skill zips
uploaded through Customize → Skills. That upload form documents a 200-character
maximum; the descriptions in SKILL.md are 439-620 characters and are the ones the
eval suite measured, so they are left alone and shortened here instead.
This file ships in no plugin and costs no context. tests/test_skill_descriptions.py
fails if a skill is missing, if a description is over 200 characters, or if it drops
a trigger phrase the README advertises.
blindspot: Blind-spot pass — find both sides' unknown unknowns before work on a plan or system, in any domain, and turn them into a better prompt. Use on "blind spot pass", "what am I missing".
brainstorm: Brainstorm the intervention — ~10 candidates for a named problem in any domain, from today to a quarter-long bet. Use on "brainstorm interventions", "show me options". NOT for design variants.
buy-in: The buy-in doc — surface what approvers don't know and will object to, answer with evidence, state limits, name who signs. Use on "buy-in doc", "prep me for review", "get sign-off".
deviation-log: Deviation log — log departures from the plan as work hits unknowns, any domain. Use on "implementation notes", "record a deviation", "where did we diverge from the plan?".
interview: The interview — before deciding, ask in rounds of ≤4 what the AI cannot know or judge about your situation. Use on "interview me", "ask me questions before implementing", "ask me before you decide".
prototypes: Prototypes — several versions of anything to react to, each on a different philosophy. Use on "divergent prototypes", "design options", "versions to react to", "know it when I see it".
quiz: Comprehension quiz — explain the work, then quiz you so you can explain and defend it at handover. Use on "quiz me", "test my understanding", or before handing over or merging.
reference: Point at a reference — read an example (a policy, proposal, product, code), show your reading for correction before building on it. Use on "use this as a reference", "make it like this".
teach-me: Teach me my unknowns — an explainer for a field's vocabulary and mental model, so vague requests become precise. Use on "teach me", "make me an explainer". Not a plan investigation.
tweakable-plan: The tweakable plan — decisions most likely to change come first, with alternatives, for any work. Use on "plan this", "make a plan", "tweakable plan".
unknowns-loop: Run the know-your-unknowns workflow end to end, ending with an outcome check. Use on "unknowns loop", "run the operating loop", "know your unknowns". A bare "loop" is NOT this.
